runtime.measurement: Accepted queue-present timestamps; physical scanout is not measured; no awake-display or physical144Hz claim

runtimeBoundary: Immutable fat jar frozen before the final total-selected-unit policy correction and honest HUD metric labels. Idle selection was well above the threshold on-screen, so the policy decision is the same there. Later source edits were not included in these measurements.

protocol.combat: 661/1000/2000 initial units × land-air/sea-air/all; 30 s initial warmup followed by three consecutive 30 s samples
protocol.idle: 2000 requested original movable unit forms, single allied team, no orders, no invulnerability or replenishment; same sampling protocol
protocol.delayProbes: 40 s each; 50 ms upload delay, 50 ms present delay, and visible=false at 15 s then restore after 10 s
protocol.measurement: Successful/suboptimal accepted vkQueuePresentKHR call timestamps. Physical scanout is not measured. Engine loops and original simulation ticks are separately recorded; this does not impose a fixed simulation step.
protocol.fiveSecondRangesScope: Native and frame diagnostic ranges omit the first startup window; these are separate diagnostic windows, not the exact 30-second scenario windows.

findings.sustained2000Idle: Three eligible windows; original unit behavior naturally creates helper/attached units, keeping 2250 living and at least 2135 visible. Accepted present FPS is 119.820–119.958; fresh snapshots 119.620–119.932 Hz; p95 8.967–9.143 ms and p99 9.344–9.490 ms. 144 FPS / 6.94 ms p95 target was not achieved.
findings.combatQualification: All nine cases exited normally but combat casualties reduce population during warmup; none qualifies as sustained 2000-unit combat. Initial populations are not reported as living populations during measurement.
findings.presentationBottleneck: Under the locked Mac/asleep 60 Hz display conditions, accepted native presentation stays near 120 Hz with immediate present mode, vsync false, target 300. A native thread sample in an earlier diagnostic run showed most render-thread waiting in CAMetalLayer nextDrawable during MoltenVK queue submission. Asynchronous MoltenVK submission moved the wait to the frame fence without removing the measured ceiling. This does not establish an awake-display hardware limit or physical 144 Hz capability.
findings.renderEngineIndependence: 50 ms upload/present delay reduces acceptance to about 16 Hz while original engine progression remains about 252–266 Hz. Resource residency remains bounded; every case exits 0 with allocator/device/instance destroyed.
findings.hiddenWindowLimitation: The frozen probe toggled the Swing JFrame only. The actual Vulkan surface uses the provided AWT canvas (CanvasWrapper/AWTVK), whose isVisible flag remained true without a canvas ComponentHidden event. Native submissions continued. This is not proof of stopped acquisition, minimized rendering, or a complete native hidden-window acceptance. The subsequent diagnostic fix explicitly hides the actual canvas and records context/window classes; it is outside this frozen matrix.
findings.shutdownWarnings: Kool allocator cleanup frees retained loading/UI mesh buffers and cached font/icon/canvas/map/atlas images at proven device-idle shutdown. These warnings remain in logs. Residency is bounded during the measured runs, but inactive-scene ownership, terminal atlas release, and final retired-texture queue draining remain cleanup work; no warning-free teardown claim.
findings.unverified: Original 1.15 two-way 10-minute mixed multiplayer interoperability, physical awake-display 144 Hz presentation, native surface-zero/minimized acquisition, and full GPU visual correctness of every hidden/transport/upgraded unit form are not established by this matrix.
findings.gpuBudget: In sustained idle capacity, native GPU timestamp averages span 6.45–7.13 ms at roughly 575–581 draw calls, near the 6.94 ms target. Native drawable waiting is observed but is not established as the sole remaining bottleneck; removing that wait alone does not prove 144 FPS.
